IMPLEMENTATION GUIDE

What to check before choosing booking management

Businesses coordinating bookable services and resources. Start by documenting the process you want the system to support, including exceptions and approval decisions. A clear process map makes it easier to assess whether the selected product supports the work through configuration or needs additional development.

Evaluate the workflow with real requirements

Use representative, approved sample data to walk through the important tasks. Ask how users find information, how permissions differ by role and what happens when a record is incomplete or a request changes. Record gaps rather than assuming that a feature name proves the workflow will work for your team.

Plan data migration and integrations

Identify the source records, duplicates, required fields and ownership of data cleanup. Define how completeness and accuracy will be checked after migration. Integrations need a documented interface, error handling and a clear owner when a connected service is unavailable. Do not assume an integration is included until the selected product and scope confirm it.

Understand cost and operational ownership

Separate subscription or licence fees from implementation, hosting, migration, training and ongoing support. Confirm who administers users and who applies updates. Ask how to export records if the business later changes platform. Ownership of the underlying software, licence conditions and source access are recorded in the commercial agreement.

Accept and hand over the system

Agree user acceptance tests before release. The final handover should identify the configured workflows, known limitations, administrator responsibilities and support route. A pilot with a representative team can expose training needs before the wider business starts using the system.
